methodPresets.name: Progressive controlled rock removal — eight steps
methodPresets.confirm: Chalmers Lane wording for Beardwood Contractors, not yet approved by TEXC for reuse (C33). Review it against this site before issuing.
methodPresets.intro: The following sequence describes TEXC's current understanding of how the work would be progressed. It is intentionally preliminary: the final methodology and site-specific controls remain subject to the exposed ground conditions, TEXC's final assessment and {client}' approval requirements.

steps.title: Make the work area safe
steps.detail: Before specialist work begins, loose or unstable material presenting an immediate risk to personnel, equipment or blasting products is to be removed, stabilised or otherwise controlled. Safe access and a suitable catchment / bund arrangement will be established where required.

steps.title: Select and expose the first rock section
steps.detail: The work will proceed progressively. TEXC and {client} will identify which exposed rock section is suitable to address first, taking into account access, surrounding structures, containment requirements and the ability to safely recover broken material after firing.

steps.title: Mark-up and drilling
steps.detail: The selected area will be marked out and drilled to suit the exposed rock geometry and the required removal outcome. Drilling results and actual hole conditions will be recorded and reviewed before the area progresses to charging.

steps.title: Final Blast Assessment
steps.detail: Following drilling, TEXC will assess the collective hole geometry, rock conditions and surrounding constraints to determine the appropriate loading and firing arrangement for the specific section. Final quantities and arrangements will be determined by the responsible shotfirer following assessment of the actual drilled and exposed conditions.

steps.title: Initiation system and containment preparation
steps.detail: The firing system will be installed and checked. Protective face spacing / separation materials, blast mats and supplementary containment will then be positioned as required.

steps.title: Enhanced matting and overburden containment
steps.detail: Where the firing location is positioned against a wall or other sensitive boundary, multiple layers of protective matting may be used. Where suitable and safe to do so, loose material may be placed over the matting as additional overburden to assist with containment of blast effects. The exact arrangement will be confirmed for each firing location.

steps.title: Controlled firing and clearance
steps.detail: The applicable exclusion, communication and firing controls will be established before the blast is initiated. The area will remain controlled until the responsible shotfirer has completed the required post-blast inspection and determined that it is safe for release.

steps.title: Mechanical extraction and repeat as required
steps.detail: Following clearance, {client}' machine will be used to extract the fragmented material and expose the next section. The same assessment, preparation, containment and firing process will be repeated as many times as necessary to safely complete the agreed rock-removal scope.

callouts.text: The work is expected to be undertaken progressively rather than as a single unrestricted blast. Each section will be treated as its own controlled work area and reassessed before progression.

siteConditions.confirm: Chalmers Lane wording for Beardwood Contractors, not yet approved by TEXC for reuse (C33). Review it against this site before issuing.
items: Exposed rock faces and significant elevation changes.
Limited areas available for equipment positioning.
Adjacent residential structures and other sensitive assets.
Existing retaining structures immediately adjacent to sections of the excavation.
Potential for displaced material to travel downslope.
Difficult access for placement and recovery of heavy protective materials.
Existing excavator operations within the work area.
Previously drilled holes containing expanding grout.
Requirement for compressed-air hoses and drilling equipment to traverse restricted areas.
Incomplete visibility of portions of the final excavation and underlying rock.

constraints.confirm: Chalmers Lane wording for Beardwood Contractors, not yet approved by TEXC for reuse (C33). Review it against this site before issuing.

rows.intent: Equipment, hoses, mats and personnel must be moved through a confined and irregular work area. Access routes and handling arrangements will be confirmed before each stage.
Loose rock and rubble are present above and around proposed work areas. Immediate hazards are to be removed or controlled before personnel or blasting products are introduced.
Residential structures, retaining elements and other sensitive assets are located close to the excavation. Containment and monitoring requirements will be assessed for each individual work area.
The terrain creates the potential for fragmented material to travel beyond the immediate firing area. Catchment / bund controls and staged extraction are intended to manage this exposure.
Protective mats are expected to be a key control. Their placement and recovery will require planning and, where practicable, mechanical assistance due to site access and mat weight.
Rubble and existing material currently obscure parts of the final rock profile. Final quantities, drilling requirements and methodology therefore cannot be fully confirmed until further exposure.

paras: This risk assessment has been prepared following an initial site inspection and is provided to {client} for review as part of the proposed works approval process.
The assessment reflects the site conditions and proposed scope visible and accessible at the time of inspection.

The excavation remains partially obscured by rubble, loose material and existing site conditions. Final work areas, drilling requirements and site-specific controls are therefore subject to verification following further exposure and preparation of the nominated areas.
**This assessment is subject to amendment where site conditions, identified hazards, scope of works or {client}' requirements change.**

riskReview.confirm: Chalmers Lane wording for Beardwood Contractors, not yet approved by TEXC for reuse (C33). Review it against this site before issuing.
paras: This document represents a **preliminary risk assessment only** and is specifically provided for {client}' review and approval.
The assessment will remain subject to review throughout preparation of the works.

Where further excavation, exposure of rock or changes to the construction site reveal conditions materially different from those observed during the initial inspection, TEXC will reassess the affected work area and amend the applicable controls before proceeding.
{client} may also request additional controls or amendments as part of its internal approval process.

It is not a final blast design or authority to undertake blasting. Final work areas, methodology and controls remain subject to further exposure, assessment and applicable approvals.

letterTemplate.confirm: Covering-letter template drafted by Brand in Black, not yet approved by TEXC (C12)
paras: Thank you for the opportunity to support {client} on the {site} works. This proposal sets out our current understanding of the work, how we would approach it, and what we would need from your team to proceed.

It is a preliminary proposal. It follows our initial site inspection and supports your review and approval process — it does not authorise blasting. Final work areas, methodology and controls will be confirmed once the site is prepared and assessed.

We work inside your systems, inductions and site procedures, and the documentation is handled as part of the job. If anything here does not match how the site actually runs, tell us and we will revise it.
